adaptation: Generalizes the existing Deuring-polynomial differentiated-operator argument to arbitrary hypergeometric parameters and a polynomial of degree less than the characteristic; extends the highest-derivative argument to an arbitrary nonzero leading coefficient and applies algebraic-closure descent. Binomial recurrences and specializations establish the two IKO parameter-polynomial cases. The two cardinality corollaries reuse the standard nodup-roots/degree proof structure.
scope_notes: Polynomial separability is proved over every field of the specified characteristic; algebraic closedness is needed only for the distinct-root counts.
g requires prime p>=5; h requires odd prime p>=3.
Endpoints, degree bounds, and the differential equations are proved rather than assumed for the IKO polynomials.
The general ODE theorem requires degree<p; a compiled characteristic-five counterexample records why.
No analytic gamma function or infinite hypergeometric series is formalized. The algebraic coefficient recurrence replaces that presentation.
No new geometric superspecial/supersingular classification or isomorphism-class counting theorem is asserted.
